newsitem.title: USA: IBM and partners develop trading system.
newsitem.headline: IBM and partners develop trading system.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp will provide the technological infrastructure in a new trading system that will allow buyers and sellers to specify a variety of trading prices and sizes while retaining anonymity, IBM and its partners in the project said Tuesday.
Partners include Colorado-based OptiMark Technologies Inc, which developed the technology, and Dow Jones & Co, which is among those funding the project.
The Pacific Stock Exchange and the Chicago Board Options Exchange have agreed to be the first exchanges to make the system available.
The system will be offered first in the equity markets and then in related options markets, the partners said.

OptiMark said it intends to offer the system non-exclusively as an integrated transaction facility for all exchanges and distribute the service through existing vendors. The system also will be accessible over the IBM Global Network, a private and secure voice, data and video network, OptiMark said.
